title: Cap. II Arg. 6: James 2:5 — poor elect / rich in faith grounds foresight-election
pass_a_gloss: The sixth testimony on which Vasquez rests is found in James 2:5: Has not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom which God has promised to those who love him? This is, the Jesuit interprets, God chose those who were poor in this world, because they were rich in faith and charity, unto glory, or the inheritance of the kingdom. Election to glory is therefore from the foreknowledge of God, who sees who at last will be rich in faith and works.
pass_b_english: Sixth: Vasquez leans on James 2:5 — "Has not God chosen the poor in this world, rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom he promised to those who love him?" The Jesuit reads it: God chose those who were poor in this world because they were rich in faith and charity — chose them to glory, the inheritance of the kingdom. So, they say, election to glory hangs on God's foresight of who will finally be rich in faith and works.
source_text: Sextum testimonium quo nititur Vasques, habetur Jacob. ii. 5. Nonne Deus elegit pauperes in hoc mundo, divites in fide, & heredes regni, quod promisit Deus diligentibus se? Hoc est, interprete Jesuita, Deus eos qui in hoc mundo pauperes erant, quia erant in fide & charitate divites, elegit ad gloriam, sive regni hereditatem. Electio igitur ad gloriam est ex praescientia Dei, qui videt quinam tandem futuri sunt divites in fide & operibus.
